other_side: Zitron argues that compute capacity exceeds demand, citing Gartner's prediction that most neoclouds will stop operating independently by 2030, and estimates over 200 billion dollars of GPUs sit in storage, though that figure is his own. He says CoreWeave's long-dated bonds yielded as much as 16 per cent and that Anthropic's reported 16.8 billion dollars of quarterly revenue sits against over 413 billion dollars of non-cancellable compute contracts. He also reports that Anthropic's IPO valuation has slipped to about 1.5 trillion dollars.
truth_beneath: The variable both men orbit is the price of money against the price of compute: whether neoclouds and labs can finance the buildout before revenue arrives. Both accept as fact that neocloud debt has repriced upward, that a Firmus listing failed, that Anthropic's valuation talk has fallen from two trillion to about one and a half trillion, and that the labs have hundreds of billions in compute commitments. The empirical question is whether this is a repricing of risk or the start of a demand shortfall; the observable is whether GPU rental prices keep rising, as the host reports, or fall, and whether any neocloud fails unrescued. The residue is worldview about whether AI revenue will broaden. For Whittemore to be vindicated, rental prices must hold and Anthropic must list successfully. For Zitron, a neocloud must fail without a backstop and growth must slow. Both are polemicists with incentives, Whittemore bullish and anti-doom, Zitron certain of a bubble and anti-hype. The signal is that both think debt markets, not technology, set the pace now. Watch the Anthropic share price on its first day.
